# Accessibility · 无障碍

The standards and laws that apply, tools that test a build, patterns that are accessible by construction, and inclusive design beyond compliance, including age-friendly design. Automated checks catch only part of the issues: keep a manual keyboard and screen-reader pass.

26 resources, plus 15 cross-listed from other domains. Columns are explained in README.md; `scripts/catalog.py find` searches every domain at once. Rows are sorted by tier, then by reach, so what an agent can fetch comes first.

## Standards and law · 标准与法规

WCAG 2.2 is the working baseline; laws (EU EAA and EN 301 549, US ADA and Section 508, China GB/T 37668 and the age-friendly rules) decide what is required where. Cite the success criterion, not a paraphrase.

## Testing tools · 检测工具

Automated checkers, browser extensions and contrast tools. Run one automated and one manual pass; a clean automated report is not proof of access.

| Resource | Best for | How to use | Tier | Kind | Reach | Access · licence | Entry point |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| [axe-core and axe DevTools](https://github.com/dequelabs/axe-core) | The most widely embedded accessibility rules engine (behind axe DevTools, Lighthouse and many CI tools); runs in any browser page or test | In a render loop, inject axe with @axe-core/playwright (or run npx @axe-core/cli <url>) and fail on serious and critical violations; each result links a rule page with the fix. Then do the manual keyboard and screen-reader pass it cannot do. | S | library | static | free · MPL-2.0 | [Rule descriptions (Deque University)](https://dequeuniversity.com/rules/axe/); [axe DevTools browser extension](https://www.deque.com/axe/devtools/); [axe MCP server (paid)](https://www.deque.com/axe/mcp-server/) |
| [WebAIM Contrast Checker (home: color)](https://webaim.org/resources/contrastchecker/) | The standard quick WCAG contrast check, with an API | API: https://webaim.org/resources/contrastchecker/?fcolor=<hex>&bcolor=<hex>&api | S | tool | static | free | API `https://webaim.org/resources/contrastchecker/?fcolor={hex}&bcolor={hex}&api` |
| [WAVE](https://wave.webaim.org) | WebAIM's evaluator that overlays errors, contrast failures and structure (headings, landmarks, ARIA) directly on the page | Deep-link a report with wave.webaim.org/report#/<url> or use the extension for pages behind login; pair it with axe, since each catches different issues. The WAVE API is paid per credit. | A | tool | static | free | [WAVE API (paid)](https://wave.webaim.org/api/) |
| [Accessibility Insights](https://accessibilityinsights.io) | Microsoft's free tools for web, Windows and Android, with a guided Assessment that walks through the manual checks automation misses | Run FastPass on every build, and the Assessment (tab stops, focus, landmarks, headings) before a release; export the report as evidence. | A | tool | static | free · MIT |  |
| [Colour Contrast Analyser (CCA)](https://vispero.com/lp/color-contrast-checker/) | Free desktop contrast checker whose eyedropper samples any pixel on screen: text over photos, gradients, screenshots and design files | Use when the colours are not in code; sample the lightest background pixel behind the text and read the WCAG AA and AAA results. | A | tool | static | free · GPL-3.0 | [Source and releases (GitHub)](https://github.com/ThePacielloGroup/CCAe) |
| [Pa11y](https://pa11y.org) | Open-source command-line accessibility tester (HTML_CodeSniffer or axe runners) with a CI variant for lists of URLs | Run npx pa11y <url> for a quick check, or pa11y-ci over a sitemap in CI; set --runner axe to match axe results elsewhere. | A | tool | static | free · LGPL-3.0 | [GitHub](https://github.com/pa11y/pa11y) |
| [NVDA screen reader](https://www.nvaccess.org) | The free, open-source Windows screen reader most used for manual testing, alongside VoiceOver on Apple devices | Do one manual pass per key flow: navigate by headings (H), landmarks (D) and form fields (F), and listen for unlabelled controls and announcements that never come. | A | tool | static | free · GPL-2.0 |  |

## Inclusive design · 包容性设计

Designing for permanent, temporary and situational disability, older users and low literacy, beyond passing a checklist.

| Resource | Best for | How to use | Tier | Kind | Reach | Access · licence | Entry point |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| [Microsoft Inclusive Design](https://inclusive.microsoft.design) | Toolkit framing disability as permanent, temporary and situational | Download the toolkit (manual and activity cards) and use the Persona Spectrum (permanent, temporary, situational) when writing a brief, so one constraint (one arm, a baby in arm, an arm injury) improves the design for all three. | A | guideline | static | free |  |
| [UK Home Office accessibility posters (multi)](https://github.com/UKHomeOffice/posters) | Do and don't posters for designing for users on the autistic spectrum, with low vision, dyslexia, anxiety, motor or hearing needs, and screen-reader users | Put the relevant poster next to the design in a critique; translations exist in many languages. | A | guideline | static | free · slow |  |
| [Inclusive Design Principles (multi)](https://inclusivedesignprinciples.info) | Seven short principles (comparable experience, consider situation, be consistent, give control, offer choice, prioritise content, add value) with examples | Use the seven headings as critique prompts for any interface, beyond pass-or-fail criteria. | A | guideline | static | free · slow |  |
